x: Savitribai Phule was India's first woman teacher, at the girls' school she and Jyotirao Phule opened in Pune in 1848.
t: Recall the Phules' girls' school.

x: Option C is incorrect: the first census was in 1872, but it was not taken everywhere at once. The first complete, synchronous census was in 1881, and 1931 was the last full caste count.
t: Discriminate the first census from the first complete census.

x: Annie Besant was the first woman INC president (1917), Sarojini Naidu the first Indian woman president (1925), Sucheta Kripalani the first woman CM, and Indira Gandhi the first woman PM. The answer is a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i.
t: Discriminate 'first woman' from 'first Indian woman'.

x: Article 17, which abolishes untouchability in any form, is the first constitutional provision against it.
t: Recall Article 17.

x: Both are true: Articles 39 and 42 first recognised family welfare in the Constitution, and India started a family-planning programme in 1952, the first in Asia (and in the world).
t: Recall the family welfare firsts.

x: The order is the Bengal Sati Regulation (1829), the Widow Remarriage Act (1856), the Child Marriage Restraint Act (1929) and the Hindu Marriage Act (1955), so the answer is B, C, D, A.
t: Arrange the reform laws in time order.

x: Auguste Comte is the father of sociology, G.S. Ghurye of Indian sociology, M.N. Srinivas of modern Indian sociology, and Irawati Karve was India's first woman sociologist. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Discriminate Ghurye from Srinivas.

x: Both are true: M.N. Srinivas coined 'Sanskritisation' and was the first to explain the 'dominant caste'. They are two separate ideas, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether two separate contributions explain each other.

x: I, II and III are correct: Verrier Elwin studied tribes, Tilka Manjhi was the first tribal freedom fighter, and Droupadi Murmu is the first ST President. IV is false because the Ministry of Tribal Affairs was set up in 1999.
t: Recall the Ministry of Tribal Affairs year, 1999.

x: Andhra State (1953) was the first state formed on linguistic lines, after Potti Sriramulu's fast unto death.
t: Recall Andhra State.

x: Article 51A(e) is the first duty promoting harmony, Nehru chaired the first National Integration Council, Potti Sriramulu fasted for a linguistic state, and Fazl Ali headed the SRC. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Match each first to its person or Article.

x: Both are true: the 1986 Act was the first comprehensive child-labour law, and the Children (Pledging of Labour) Act, 1933, was the first child-labour law. An earlier law does not explain a later one, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether an earlier law explains a later one.

x: Both are true: Article 24, banning child labour in hazardous work, was the first constitutional protection for children, and the RTE Act came in 2009.
t: Recall the child-rights firsts.

x: Jayaprakash Narayan led the JP Movement (1974), the first major youth movement after Independence. Derozio led the much earlier Young Bengal movement.
t: Discriminate pre- and post-Independence youth movements.

x: The Community Development Programme began in 1952, the National Extension Service in 1953, the NREP in 1980 and the NSAP in 1995. The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Arrange the welfare programmes in time order.

x: Three are correct: the NCW (1992), the Maternity Benefit Act (1961) and the Equal Remuneration Act (1976). The National Mission for Empowerment of Women began in 2010; 2015 is Beti Bachao Beti Padhao.
t: Discriminate 2010 from 2015.

x: Kalelkar headed the first Backward Classes Commission, B.P. Mandal chaired the second, the Mandal Commission recommended 27%, and the 102nd Amendment (2018) gave the NCBC constitutional status. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Discriminate the person from the commission.

x: Both are true: the RPwD Act, 2016, was the first rights-based disability law, and the PwD Act, 1995, the first comprehensive one. An earlier law does not explain a later one, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether an earlier law explains a later one.

x: The order is Kalelkar (1953), NCW (1992), NHRC (1993) and NCPCR (2007), so the answer is B, C, A, D.
t: Arrange the bodies in time order.

x: All four are correct: Irawati Karve first studied the Indian family systematically in 'Kinship Organization in India', Articles 39 and 42 recognised family welfare, and India's 1952 family-planning programme was the world's first.
t: Recall the family firsts.

x: The Phules opened the first girls' school, Vidyasagar led the widow-remarriage movement, the Widow Remarriage Act came in 1856, and Raja Ram Mohan Roy led the campaign against sati. The answer is a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.
t: Match each reform to its leader or law.

x: The Brahmo Samaj (1828) counts as both the first social and the first religious reform movement, founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy. The Justice Party (1916) is counted as the first caste association. The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Note the Brahmo Samaj fills two slots.

x: The National Commission for Minorities was first set up in 1992, the separate NCSC in 2004, the first child-labour law in 1933, and the first Juvenile Justice Act in 1986. The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Match each first to its year.

x: All three are correct: the first National Policy for Children came in 1974, the National Policy for Women in 2001, and the National Education Policy in 1968.
t: Recall the first policy years.

x: Both are true: Tamil Nadu started the Mid-Day Meal Scheme, so it was the first State to introduce it.
t: Recall the Mid-Day Meal pioneer.

x: Both are true: the Right to Equality was the first Fundamental Right enforced, and the First Amendment came in 1951. The date of an amendment does not explain which right came first, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a date explains a first.

x: The 65th Amendment gave the SC Commission constitutional status, Kalelkar was the first OBC commission, Bombay University had the first sociology department (1919), and Ghurye is the first Indian sociologist. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Match each first to its holder.

x: All four are correct: Irawati Karve wrote 'Kinship Organization in India' (1953), divided India into kinship zones, and was the first Indian scholar of kinship.
t: Recall Irawati Karve.

x: Irawati Karve first drew out the differences between north and south Indian kinship. Ghurye studied caste and race, and Risley classified caste.
t: Recall Irawati Karve.

x: The Age of Consent Act (1891) was the first legal step against child marriage, Vidyasagar championed widow remarriage, Ram Mohan Roy opposed sati, and the Special Marriage Act of 1872 came first. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Match each first to its holder.

x: Both are true: Karve's 'Kinship Organization in India' was the first landmark kinship study, and Ghurye first linked kinship with caste. Ghurye's work does not explain Karve's book, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether two scholars' work explain each other.

x: Herbert Risley first defined caste scientifically, G.S. Ghurye first studied it systematically, and Ghurye's 'Caste and Race in India' (1932) was the first major book on it. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Discriminate Risley from Ghurye.

x: All four are correct: Shahu Maharaj began the first reservation policy in Kolhapur State in 1902, IGNTU was the first tribal university, and Droupadi Murmu is the first tribal woman President.
t: Recall the reservation and tribal firsts.

x: Both are true: the first draft National Tribal Policy was prepared in 2006, and G.S. Ghurye first studied ethnicity and culture in India.
t: Recall the tribal and ethnicity firsts.

x: The SRC (1953) was the first linguistic reorganisation commission, the Andhra movement the first ethnic movement to win a state, Chhattisgarh the first new state of 2000, and the 7th Amendment (1956) indirectly addressed regional imbalance. The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Match each first to its event.

x: All five are correct: Articles 15(4) and 16(4), Kolhapur's 1902 reservation by Shahu Maharaj, the First Amendment (1951) and Article 338 are each the first in their line for SCs and STs.
t: Recall the reservation firsts.

x: The National Integration Council began in 1961, Articles 29 and 30 first protected minority rights, the Communal Award came in 1932, and the National Foundation for Communal Harmony in 1992. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv.
t: Match each first to its year or Article.

x: All four are correct: Ram Mohan Roy led the campaign against sati, Vidyasagar the push for widow remarriage, and the 2005 and 2013 Acts were the first domestic-violence law and the post-Nirbhaya amendment.
t: Recall the women's reform firsts.

x: The first National Policy for Women came in 2001, the first domestic-violence law in 2005, the post-Nirbhaya amendment in 2013, and Kiran Bedi was the first woman IPS officer. The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Match each first to its holder.

x: M. Fathima Beevi (1989) was the first woman judge of the Supreme Court. Kiran Bedi was the first woman IPS officer and Pratibha Patil the first woman President.
t: Match each first to the woman who holds it.

x: The first JJ Act came in 1986, the 86th Amendment (2002) made education a Fundamental Right, India ratified the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child in 1992, and Childline is 1098. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Match each first to its holder.

x: The Swadeshi movement (1905) was the first student-led national movement, Young Bengal the first youth organisation, founded by Derozio, and the JP movement (1974) the first after Independence. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Match each youth first to its holder.

x: All five are correct: India Against Corruption (2011), the first Youth Policy (1988), and the first National Youth Day and youth ministry (both 1985). Youth Day, 12 January, marks Swami Vivekananda's birthday.
t: Recall the youth firsts.

x: The NCPCR was set up in 2007, the separate NCSC and NCST both in 2004, and the First Plan ran 1951–56. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Match each body to its year.

x: Both are true: the First Plan focused on welfare, and it ran from 1951 to 1956. A date range does not explain a plan's focus, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a date explains a character.

x: The Rural Works Programme (1970s) was the first anti-poverty programme, the IRDP pilot began in 1976, the PDS was the first food-security programme, and MGNREGA (2005) the first rights-based welfare law. The answer is a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.
t: Match each first to its holder.

x: All three are correct: the first National Health Policy came in 1983, the Population Policy in 1976, and the Nutrition Policy in 1993.
t: Recall the first policy years.

x: Articles 29 and 30 were the first safeguards for minorities, Justice Mohammed Sardar Ali Khan the first NCM chairman, Article 30 the first minority education right, and the Ranganath Misra Commission the first on religious and linguistic minorities. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Discriminate Articles 29–30 from Article 30 alone.

x: All four are correct: the NCM and the National Foundation for Communal Harmony date from 1992, the 15-Point Programme from 1983, and the Sachar Committee from 2005.
t: Recall the minority firsts.

x: The first women's policy came in 2001, Jayanti Patnaik was the first NCW chairperson, the Domestic Violence Act came in 2005, and Article 15(3) was the first safeguard for women. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Match each first to its holder.

x: Both are true: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao began in 2015, and the 73rd and 74th Amendments first reserved local-body seats for women. They are unrelated, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether two unrelated facts explain each other.

x: The first National Policy for Persons with Disabilities came in 2006, the PWD Act, 1995 created the Chief Commissioner, the National Trust Act came in 1999, and DPSPs and equality provisions are the constitutional basis. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Match each first to its holder.

x: The first multi-disability national institute for empowering persons with disabilities was set up in 2005. 1999 is the National Trust Act and 2006 the disability policy.
t: Discriminate the disability firsts by year.

x: The first National Policy for Children came in 1974, the NCPCR was set up in 2007 with Shanta Sinha as first chair, and the first JJ Act came in 1986. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv.
t: Match each first to its holder.

x: Childline is 1098, ICDS (1975) the first integrated child-development programme, the NCBC became a constitutional body in 2018, and the NCW was set up in 1992. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Match each first to its holder.

x: All three are correct: separate national commissions for SCs and STs were first set up in 2004, after the 89th Amendment, and the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities was the first disability-rights body.
t: Recall the 2004 split.

x: The Bengal Sati Regulation (1829) was the first law against sati, Bharat Stree Mahamandal (1910) the first women's organisation, Sarojini Naidu the first woman Governor, and Pratibha Patil the first woman President. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Match each first to its holder.

x: All three are correct: the First Amendment (1951) first recognised OBC reservation, the first NCBC came in 1993, and Kolhapur was the first State to bring in reservation.
t: Recall the OBC firsts.

x: The Justice Party (1916, Madras) was the first regional political party. The Andhra movement and Young Bengal were movements, and the Brahmo Samaj a reform society.
t: Discriminate a party from a movement.

x: The NCM dates from 1992 and the NHRC from 1993, so only the key fits a and b. The NCW was in fact also set up in 1992, so c-iii (2004, the year of the separate NCSC) is a flaw in the question. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii.
t: Fix the certain pairs first, then eliminate.

x: I and II are correct: the Kalelkar Commission (1953) was the first Backward Classes Commission, with Kaka Kalelkar as chairman. III is false because B.P. Mandal chaired the second commission.
t: Discriminate the First and Second Commissions.

x: The Sarda Act (Child Marriage Restraint Act, 1929) was the first law restraining child marriage. The Age of Consent Act, 1891, was an earlier measure but not a restraint law.
t: Discriminate the 1891 and 1929 laws.

x: The Justice Party (1916) is counted as the first caste association, out of the non-Brahmin movement. The Brahmo Samaj was a reform society, and Bharat Stree Mahamandal a women's body.
t: Match each first to its holder.

x: Both are true: India's National Family Planning Programme of 1952 was the first in the world, so it was also the first in Asia. R explains A.
t: Ask whether 'first in the world' explains 'first in Asia'.

x: Both are true: the Special Marriage Act, 1872, was the first special marriage law, and the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, the first codified Hindu marriage law after Independence.
t: Discriminate the 1872 and 1955 laws.

x: All three are correct: the PDS was the first food-security programme, the NSAP began in 1995, and MGNREGA (2005) was the first rights-based welfare law.
t: Recall the welfare firsts.

x: Bombay University had the first sociology department, Sachar was the first data-based committee on minorities, Ranganath Misra the first commission on religious and linguistic minorities, and the Ministry of Tribal Affairs the first tribal ministry. The answer is a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.
t: Match each first to its holder.

x: Indira Gandhi National Tribal University (Amarkantak, 2007) was India's first tribal university.
t: Recall the first tribal university.

x: Two belong to 1985: the first National Youth Day and the youth ministry. The first Youth Policy came in 1988 and the first Education Policy in 1968.
t: Recall each youth first's year.

x: The National Foundation for Communal Harmony was set up in 1992. 1983 is the 15-Point Programme and 2005 the Sachar Committee.
t: Recall the minority firsts by year.

x: Kiran Bedi was the first woman IPS officer, the post-Nirbhaya amendment came in 2013, the women's policy in 2001, and the women's empowerment mission in 2010. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Match each first to its holder.

x: The first National Nutrition Policy came in 1993. 1983 is the Health Policy and 1976 the Population Policy.
t: Recall the first policy years.

x: The Ministry of Welfare was set up in 1985 and renamed Social Justice and Empowerment in 1998. Tribal Affairs was split off in 1999 and Minority Affairs in 2006. The answer is A, B, C, D.
t: Arrange the ministry changes in time order.

x: Social Justice handles transgender welfare, Tribal Affairs the Forest Rights Act, Minority Affairs the Parsis and other minorities, and WCD the Poshan schemes. The answer is a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i.
t: Match each subject to its ministry.

x: Both are true: WCD handles child welfare, and Social Justice handles SC welfare. One ministry's work does not explain another's, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether two ministries explain each other.

x: Option B is incorrect: the Poshan schemes come under Women and Child Development. Minority Affairs deals with the six notified minorities.
t: Match each subject to its ministry.

x: Both are true: Social Justice and Empowerment handles OBC welfare, and Christians are one of the six minorities under Minority Affairs.
t: Match each subject to its ministry.

x: Social Justice and Empowerment handles persons with disabilities, through its Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities.
t: Match each group to its ministry.

x: All three are correct: the Ministry of Tribal Affairs handles Scheduled Tribes, putting PESA into effect, and tribal education and development.
t: Recall the Tribal Affairs ministry's work.

x: Senior citizens' welfare comes under Social Justice and Empowerment, which runs the Senior Citizens Act, 2007.
t: Match each group to its ministry.

x: Transgender persons' welfare comes under Social Justice and Empowerment, which runs the Transgender Persons Act, 2019.
t: Match each group to its ministry.

x: Tribal education and development comes under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs. Women's empowerment, child protection and Poshan come under WCD.
t: Match each subject to its ministry.

x: Buddhists are one of the six notified minorities under Minority Affairs, along with Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Parsis and Jains.
t: Recall the six notified minorities.

x: Option B is incorrect: Hindus are not a notified national minority. Minority Affairs covers Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis and Jains.
t: Recall the six notified minorities.

x: Both are true: WCD handles child protection and the Poshan schemes. They are two separate tasks, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether two tasks explain each other.

x: Social Justice handles senior citizens, Tribal Affairs the FRA, Minority Affairs the Christians, and WCD the Poshan schemes. The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Match each subject to its ministry.

x: Both are true: Christians and Jains are both notified minorities under Minority Affairs. Jains were added in 2014.
t: Recall the six notified minorities.

x: All five areas come under WCD: women's empowerment, child welfare, ICDS, Poshan schemes and child protection. 'All six' is a trap, as only five are listed.
t: Count the listed items.

x: All three are correct: Parsis come under Minority Affairs, child protection under WCD, and the FRA under Tribal Affairs.
t: Match each subject to its ministry.

x: All four are today's successor ministries: Social Justice and Empowerment, Tribal Affairs, Minority Affairs, and Women and Child Development.
t: Recall today's social-sector ministries.

x: PM-AJAY merges Adarsh Gram, Special Central Assistance to the SC Sub-Plan, and the Babu Jagjivan Ram hostel scheme, all for SCs. The other options are tribal, women's and minority schemes.
t: Recall the schemes merged into PM-AJAY.

x: Option C is incorrect: covering 75 PVTG communities through 11 key interventions is PM-JANMAN. PM-VIKAS supports the six notified minorities.
t: Match each target to its scheme.

x: Both are true: SHRESHTA places meritorious SC students in residential education at top private schools, and that is who the scheme is for. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the target group explains the provision.

x: Both are true: the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam reserves 33% of Lok Sabha and Assembly seats for women, and it is the 106th Amendment. The Act's number does not explain what it provides, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether an Act's number explains its content.

x: PM-YASASVI is the scholarship and hostel scheme for OBCs, EBCs and DNTs, SEED empowers DNTs economically, ADIP gives assistive devices, and Mission Vatsalya covers child protection. The answer is a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
t: Match each scheme to its purpose.

x: All four are correct: Mission Shakti has Sambal and Samarthya, POSHAN 2.0 has Poshan Tracker and Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi, Ujjwala gives LPG in women's names, and UDID gives one disability card.
t: Recall the components of each scheme.

x: Both are true: the Sickle Cell Mission aims to end sickle-cell anaemia by 2047, and Naya Savera and Nai Udaan give minority students free coaching and support after UPSC or SSC prelims.
t: Recall the target year 2047.

x: Three are for women: Mission Shakti, the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam and Ujjwala. Mission Vatsalya is for children.
t: Find the scheme for children.

x: NAMASTE, now with SMILE, aims at mechanised sanitation, zero deaths from manual scavenging, and rehabilitation of sanitation workers.
t: Match each scheme to its purpose.

x: PM-AJAY, the Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana, is for Scheduled Castes. PM-JANMAN is for PVTGs, and Naya Savera for minorities.
t: Expand the short name.

x: All three are correct: PM-JANMAN (PM Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan) is for STs, especially PVTGs, and its key interventions include housing, roads, water and electricity.
t: Recall the PM-JANMAN target and interventions.

x: Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan is led by Tribal Affairs, working with several other ministries to bring basic facilities to tribal-majority villages.
t: Match each scheme to its lead ministry.

x: EMRS comes under Tribal Affairs, the Sickle Cell Mission screens tribal people, PM-YASASVI comes under Social Justice, and Naya Savera under Minority Affairs. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Match each scheme to its ministry or focus.

x: All four are SEED support areas for DNTs: health insurance, housing, livelihoods and coaching for competitive exams.
t: Recall SEED's four areas.

x: Samarthya is Mission Shakti's empowerment part, PMMVY gives maternity benefit, Sakhi Niwas runs working women's hostels, and Palna runs crèches. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Match each scheme to its purpose.

x: The Nari Shakti Act comes under Law & Justice, Ujjwala under Petroleum, Childline 1098 is linked with 112 under Mission Vatsalya, and Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi covers early childhood education. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Match each scheme to its detail.

x: Both are true: POSHAN 2.0 uses technology (Poshan Tracker) to monitor nutrition, and it covers children aged 0–6. The age group does not explain the use of technology, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a target group explains a method.

x: Both are true: the Accessible India Campaign is Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan, and the Unique Disability ID (UDID) comes under Social Justice & Empowerment.
t: Recall the disability schemes.

x: The ADIP scheme (Assistance to Disabled Persons for aids and appliances) comes under Social Justice & Empowerment.
t: Match each scheme to its ministry.

x: PM-VIKAS stands for PM Virasat Ka Samvardhan, a Minority Affairs scheme. The other options expand PM-AJAY, PM-JANMAN and EMRS.
t: Expand the short name.

x: All three are correct: PM-VIKAS brings together skill training, support for artisans and entrepreneurship for minorities.
t: Recall the three PM-VIKAS components.

x: Both are true: EMRS gives good middle and high school education in remote areas because it is meant for tribal students who live there. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the target group explains the provision.

x: Both are true: the Sickle Cell Mission is run by Health & Family Welfare with Tribal Affairs, and it focuses on screening tribal populations.
t: Recall the Sickle Cell Mission.

x: Dharti Aaba comes under Tribal Affairs, Naya Savera and Nai Udaan under Minority Affairs, Ujjwala under Petroleum, and ADIP under Social Justice. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv.
t: Match each scheme to its ministry.

x: Clean water is one of PM-JANMAN's key interventions, with housing, roads and electricity. LPG is Ujjwala, coaching is Naya Savera, and JJ homes are Mission Vatsalya.
t: Match each provision to its scheme.

x: Option A is incorrect: Naya Savera and Nai Udaan support minority students who clear the UPSC or SSC prelims, not the mains.
t: Watch for 'Main' replacing 'prelims'.

x: I, II and III are correct: Mission Vatsalya covers child protection, foster care and juvenile justice homes. IV is false because LPG in women's names is Ujjwala.
t: Match each provision to its scheme.

x: Both are true: Ujjwala improves women's health by giving LPG connections in their names, which ends indoor smoke from wood fires. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the means explains the aim.

x: PM-YASASVI comes under Social Justice, PM-VIKAS under Minority Affairs, and both Mission Shakti and Mission Vatsalya under WCD. The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv.
t: Match each scheme to its ministry.

x: Three come under WCD: Mission Shakti, Mission Vatsalya and POSHAN 2.0. PM-VIKAS comes under Minority Affairs.
t: Find the non-WCD scheme.

x: Both are true: UDID gives one national database and ID card for disability benefits, and ADIP gives modern assistive devices free.
t: Recall the disability schemes.

x: Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan aims to bring full basic facilities to about 63,000 tribal-majority villages. 75 is PM-JANMAN's PVTG count and 11 its interventions.
t: Discriminate 63,000 villages from 75 PVTGs.

x: I, II and III are correct: POSHAN 2.0 has Poshan Tracker and Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi, and covers ages 0–6. IV is false because it comes under WCD, not Minority Affairs.
t: Match each scheme to its ministry.

x: All three are correct: PM-AJAY and SEED come under Social Justice and Empowerment, and PM-JANMAN under Tribal Affairs with other ministries.
t: Match each scheme to its ministry.

x: Both are true: Sambal, Mission Shakti's safety part, focuses on safety because it covers One Stop Centres, the 112 emergency system and Beti Bachao Beti Padhao. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the components explain the focus.

x: All three are covered: the Accessible India Campaign makes buildings, transport and ICT accessible. 'All four' is a trap, as only three are listed.
t: Count the listed items.

x: The Accessible India Campaign is run by Social Justice and Empowerment (Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities).
t: Match each scheme to its ministry.
